Chief_Complaint.content: Patient presents with a persistent cough and runny nose for the last 5-6 days.
Chief_Complaint.source_text: I've just been having this like, cough, for quite a few days. And my nose is running... I think it started like maybe, a bit less than a week ago. Like maybe, maybe five or six days ago.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: The cough is dry, continuous, and keeps the patient awake at night.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: It's quite dry. And it's just all day, it like keeps me up at night as well, which is really annoying.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient has a sore throat, which she attributes to irritation from coughing.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: the coughing is giving me a sore throat. But it's not like, you know not more than, than that.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient denies ear pain, ear blockage, or chest pain.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Nothing, nothing on the ears... Any pain in your chest? No not, not that either.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient does not feel short of breath at rest but feels generally tired.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Day to day when you walk around, uh you don't feel breathless do you? I don't feel restless. No, I feel you know, generally tired.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient has been experiencing shivers and feeling cold, suggesting a fever, but has not measured a temperature.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I've been having like, like shivers, even when I'm in, when I'm in bed... I haven't taken my temperature

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports significant muscle pain (myalgia) in the arms and legs, making her want to stay in bed.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: My muscle was really hurting... Especially like in my arms, my legs, like just everywhere basically.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient had a brief episode of diarrhea at the start of the illness, which has now resolved.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I had a little bit of diarrhea... Yeah, yeah. It got better.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient denies nausea or vomiting and reports a normal appetite.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: No. No, no nausea. No vomiting... I mean it's OK.

Past_Medical_History.source_text: well I have type two diabetes.
And I have quite high blood pressure.

Medications.source_text: I take Metformin for the diabetes.

Medications.content: Patient takes Lisinopril for high blood pressure.
Medications.source_text: And I take Lisinopril for the high blood pressure.

Family_History.source_text: Uh my dad also has type two diabetes.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient is 50 years old and lives with her partner.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: my name is April, and I'm fifty... it's just me and my partner.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient works as a developer in the IT field.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: I am a developer... Work in IT.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient is an ex-smoker, having quit six months ago.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: I used to, but I've stopped for about six months now.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient drinks 2-3 glasses of wine on 3 evenings per week (approx. 12-18 units/week).
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: I don't drink more than like, like, let's say three evenings a week?... I'd say like maybe two or three glasses.

Assessment.content: The impression is a viral illness / upper respiratory tract infection (URTI).
Assessment.source_text: I think uh essentially I think you're, you're going through a bit of a bit of a viral illness.

Plan_of_Care.content: Advised supportive management including bed rest and drinking plenty of fluids.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: get some nice, good rest. Drink plenty of fluids.

Plan_of_Care.content: Advised to take 1-2 days off work.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: I would say maybe take a day or two off work, if you can.

Plan_of_Care.content: A potential for antibiotics was discussed if symptoms do not improve.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: if you are still feeling feverish, um and your cough isn't getting any better, then we may look to give you some antibiotics for your chest.

Follow_up_Information.content: Patient to return for review in 2-3 days if not getting better.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: If you feel like you're still not getting any better in two to three days, it's probably worth coming back to see me again.

Follow_up_Information.content: Advised to return sooner if cough worsens or breathing becomes more difficult.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: if your cough isn't getting any better, or your breathing is getting worse, I want you to come back and see me sooner.
